summary_paragraph: A homeless man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, and chronic hepatitis C presented with worsening right toe pain, discoloration, and symptoms of heart failure including shortness of breath, leg swelling, and orthopnea. He had been non-adherent with antibiotics from a prior admission. Evaluation showed no acute infection or cardiopulmonary disease; X-rays revealed unchanged chronic osteomyelitis. Podiatry recommended no antibiotics or procedure, attributing the toe changes to chronic eschar and microvascular disease. He was treated for acute on chronic heart failure with increased furosemide and monitored for renal function, which improved with diuresis. Due to patient preference, he was discharged after one day with a plan for outpatient follow-up, despite not being fully optimized. Discharge included medication adjustments and instructions for weight monitoring and prompt follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
